title: Fresh everyday-life regenerative formation sensing after demoting generic hidden-asset discovery
purpose: Restart from a white active portfolio and sense ordinary-life potential gradients without carrying hidden-asset discovery, gigs, products or explicit tasks as priors.
governing_truth: ONE FAILED FORMATION != FAILED CALIBRATION FAMILY
scan_scope: shared physical space and neighborhood integration

formation_zones.name: Age-segmented community infrastructure × all-age recurring everyday demand

potential_a.label: elder-oriented/community fixed infrastructure
potential_a.disequilibrium: many elder-service facilities need higher utilization and more sustainable operating economics while preserving elder-service priority

potential_b.label: young workers / parents / students / general residents
potential_b.disequilibrium: daily need for affordable, healthy, close-to-home meals and neighborhood third spaces; working families also face cooking/time pressure

partial_flows.fact: Yancheng Tinghu's elder canteens have expanded into all-age canteens serving older adults, young office workers and children; operators extend service hours and adjust menus to fit workers/children.

Shanghai Ganquan's elder canteen explicitly frames all-age traffic as a way to reduce subsidy dependence and pursue 'self-generated operating blood'; it attracts surrounding office workers and uses afternoon idle periods for cooking classes.
Beijing Tongyun and Taizhou Hailing similarly report elder canteens becoming all-age shared kitchens with extended hours and continued youth/family demand.

demand_pump: fixed-capacity economics recur every operating day
formation_zones.candidate_missing_edge: time-slot / menu / pricing / programming / access design that lets age-specific fixed assets serve complementary all-age demand without crowding out protected users
contradiction: current public/community and third-party operators already perform this conversion
the underlying function resembles ordinary foodservice / space operations rather than a hidden new market
subsidies and public rent/space can materially change economics
foodservice regulation and local foot traffic dominate outcome
formation_zones.verdict: Use as a canonical life-world regenerative benchmark. The river is real, but generic operation is already visible and maturing; no open edge is evidenced.

formation_zones.name: Rare-use household/community assets × recurring episodic micro-needs

potential_a.label: idle physical household/community assets
potential_a.disequilibrium: households purchase/store assets used only a few times; items occupy space while identical needs recur nearby

potential_b.label: neighbors with episodic household needs
potential_b.disequilibrium: buying a whole asset for one small repair/use is expensive and wasteful; professional call-out fees can exceed the value of the task

partial_flows.fact: People's Daily in Aug 2026 explicitly described the recurring household pattern: drill/pipe wrench/pump needed for tiny repairs, buying is uneconomic and professional call-out fees can be disproportionate; it proposed neighborhood shared toolboxes.
Multiple current communities operate shared tool stations/houses; residents donate idle tools and borrow them through registration.
A Ningbo community expanded the circulation set beyond tools to strollers, rehabilitation wheelchairs and other rarely used household items.

demand_pump: household repairs and one-off use cases recur continuously across many households
new residents repeatedly create setup/repair needs
formation_zones.candidate_missing_edge: local inventory visibility + custody/maintenance + simple borrowing rules; for skill-dependent items, access to someone who knows how to use them
contradiction: the basic missing edge is simple and already being solved with physical shared stations
multiple software prototypes already reproduce LBS inventory/borrowing
maintenance/liability/custody can consume much of private surplus
community/property is a natural low-cost operator
formation_zones.verdict: Real regenerative circulation, but weak private whitespace and low economic density. Keep as benchmark, not active candidate.

formation_zones.name: Workday household absence × persistent neighborhood local presence

potential_a.label: working-age / mobile / young households
state_pressure: adults are physically absent for long workday periods
many households have pets, deliveries, repair appointments, plants, children or older family members requiring occasional local presence
new-city/young households often have weak nearby family networks

potential_b.label: low-age retirees / home-based residents / long-term neighbors

partial_flows.fact: Current community mutual-aid systems repeatedly route very small local needs such as package pickup, appliance repair, item purchase and other doorstep services to nearby residents with time/skills.

A Beijing community has two retirees in their seventies performing frequent mobile neighborhood repair, showing persistent local presence plus practical skill already becoming a repeated micro-service flow.
A Shenzhen community moved from lending tools to recruiting local skilled residents because residents often had tools but lacked the practical ability to solve small household problems.
Young/new-resident communities report weak local familiar networks and recurring reliance on organized local volunteers/services for childcare, elder support and everyday needs.

recurring_event_source: young/new-city migration repeatedly creates households without nearby kin
retirement continually replenishes daytime local presence

missing_edge_hypotheses.label: GENERIC NEIGHBOR MATCHING
missing_edge_hypotheses.reason: Numerous community platforms, commercial last-mile services and current app prototypes already offer local task matching.

missing_edge_hypotheses.label: TRUSTED STANDING LOCAL PROXY
missing_edge_hypotheses.statement: The deeper edge may be not one-task matching but a persistent, permissioned local person/relationship able to absorb heterogeneous small household presence events over time.
missing_edge_hypotheses.caution: Current evidence shows workarounds but does not prove households want one standing proxy, that retirees want the role, or that liability/boundary can be standardized.

incumbents_and_counterevidence.fact: Commercial last-mile/community-service operators already offer package pickup, local delivery, pet care, home service and skill sharing.
Multiple current product prototypes explicitly target the same neighborhood micro-task gradient with LBS matching, identity review, payment and ratings.
incumbents_and_counterevidence.evidence_role: idea/competition evidence, not proof of commercial adoption

incumbents_and_counterevidence.fact: Mutual-aid eldercare policy explicitly institutionalizes low-age retirees and local residents as neighborhood support supply, reducing whitespace in elder-support subdomains.

formation_zones.decisive_next_evidence: Do not build a neighborhood task platform. Search whether families repeatedly rely on the same trusted nearby person across multiple heterogeneous household events; whether that relationship persists across months/years; what causes it to form; and what breaks when the person is unavailable. Kill if the pattern reduces to existing property/home-service/task marketplaces.

formation_zones.name: Young/new-city weak local roots × aging-neighborhood stable social capital and underused space

potential_a.label: young migrants / new-city residents
state_pressure: need for affordable housing, third space and belonging

potential_b.label: older neighborhoods / long-term residents
state_pressure: declining/underused common areas in some neighborhoods
need for new foot traffic and participation

partial_flows.fact: Shanghai Pengpu embedded a roughly 2,000-person youth rental community inside an older residential area; young renters use old-neighborhood shops/public spaces and interact naturally with long-term residents through shared daily routines and pet/social spaces.
Current community-space redesigns repeatedly turn underused corners/overhead spaces into shared living rooms, night-school or hobby spaces run by a mix of young residents and retired residents.

recurring_event_source: daily need for food, leisure, study, pets and social contact
underused local spaces recur as neighborhood stock
formation_zones.candidate_missing_edge: low-pressure repeated co-presence/routines and shared spaces that let stable local social capital and young demand meet without formal matching
contradiction: community/real-estate operators already intentionally design this
value capture may accrue mainly to landlords, retail and public-space operators rather than the intergenerational relationship
the edge may simply be urban design/community operations
social benefit can be high with no distinct private orchestration layer
formation_zones.verdict: Interesting life-world formation sensor, but commercial missing edge is weak/unbound. Keep as secondary research zone.

cross_zone_learning: Fresh life-world sensing produces several real regenerative flows, but most obvious surface mechanisms are already being institutionalized by community/property/service operators.
The strongest recurring ordinary-life gradients are often about time, location and fixed-asset utilization rather than hidden talent.

Young × retired remains visible most strongly through asymmetric local presence: working-age households leave the neighborhood during the day while retirees/long-term residents remain locally available.
Generic matching is not a viable new thesis; it is already crowded and repeatedly reinvented.
The only still-interesting deeper question in FLW-013-C is whether repeated household absence produces a durable 'trusted standing local proxy' relationship rather than isolated tasks.
FLW-013-A and FLW-013-B are useful benchmarks: they show how ordinary-life circulation becomes obvious once the resource and repeated event are simple enough.

active_formation_zones: FLW-013-C workday household absence × persistent neighborhood local presence
secondary_research_zones: FLW-013-D young/new-city weak roots × aging-neighborhood social capital
benchmark_maturing_flows: FLW-013-B rare-use household assets × episodic micro-needs

next_action: Deepen only FLW-013-C at the relationship/workaround layer. Search ordinary households that repeatedly rely on the same nearby non-kin person for heterogeneous daytime presence events (pet, parcel, repair access, plant/home check, child/elder micro-support), persistence over time, permission/boundary/compensation patterns, and counterevidence from property/home-service platforms. Do not search one-off gigs. Kill FLW-013-C if the recurrent unit remains one task rather than one durable local relationship.
